title: Derived termwise global sections with finite evaluation and transition normalization
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ an inverse sequence of sheaves of commutative rings. Write $\mathscr S(B)$ for strict semilinear systems of module sheaves, with componentwise exactness, identified with modules over $B$ on the sequence site $\mathcal T=\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\ge1}$ [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]. Use unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $A$ be a sheaf of commutative rings with compatible maps $A\to B_n$. Let $U:D(\mathscr S(B))\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(A)))$ be exact termwise scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. The termwise global-sections functor on constant-$A$ towers has a total right derived functor $R\Gamma^{\operatorname{Tow}}_{\mathcal C}$, computed by a K-injective resolution in the constant-$A$ tower category [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Consequently $$G=R\Gamma^{\operatorname{Tow}}_{\mathcal C}\circ U:D(\mathscr S(B))\longrightarrow D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab}))$$ is an actual functor on the ordinary derived category of strict systems. There are specified natural isomorphisms $$e_nG(J)\cong R\Gamma(\mathcal C,\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B_n}J_n)\cong R\Gamma(\mathcal C,J_n),$$ the last expression computed in $B_n$-modules and then regarded as an abelian complex. The first comparison is induced by evaluating the same constant-$A$ tower resolution; the second is the derived direct-image composition comparison for scalar restriction followed by global sections. These isomorphisms intertwine the actual tower transitions with the maps of derived sections induced by $J_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{B_{n+1}\to B_n}J_n$. They are natural for input derived morphisms. No assertion that varying-ring evaluation preserves K-injectives is made.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(A)$ and $\mathcal V=\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)$. Restriction along any coefficient-ring map changes only the action, so preserves the sectionwise kernels and the sheafified sectionwise cokernels described in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus the componentwise functor $U^0:\mathscr S(B)\to\mathcal V$ is exact, by the assumed componentwise exactness and [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Compatibility of $A\to B_n$ makes every transition $A$-linear. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], $U^0$ induces the asserted functor $U$ on ordinary derived categories. Its evaluations are the termwise restrictions of the input evaluations; this follows degree by degree from [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars].

source.place: Module-sheaf kernels and cokernels; exact restriction of the scalar action. The argument is written out using the cited module-category statement.

proof.text: The category $\mathcal V$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-small-module-diagrams-grothendieck], with index the small countable category $\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{op}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-functorial-existence] to obtain a functorial resolution $P\to I(P)$ of every complex of constant-$A$ towers. The individual module-sheaf categories also have K-injective resolutions by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Here the site is small and all ring sheaves and tower indices lie in the chosen coefficient universe, as required by these statements. No boundedness or exactness of infinite products is required.

source.place: Tag 079P, theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck, applied to the small diagram module category.

proof.text: Let $H^0:\mathcal V\to\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab})$ send a tower to its tower of global sections, using the actual transition maps. It is additive: the maps on sections preserve addition, and finite biproducts and their maps are componentwise. Applying an additive functor degreewise respects homotopies, shifts and mapping cones (a cone uses only a finite biproduct in each degree); hence it gives an exact functor $K(\mathcal V)\to D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab}))$. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] now hold by Step 2. Obtain $R H^0=R\Gamma^{\operatorname{Tow}}_{\mathcal C}$ with its universal unit, computed by $H^0I(P)$. Define $G=(R H^0)U$. This composition is a functor on the ordinary derived category, since both factors are functors there; it is not merely a choice of objects at each level.

source.place: Tags 070I and 070Y: K-injective computation and existence of the total right derived functor.

proof.text: For a complex $P$ of constant-$A$ towers, the resolution $P\to I$ of Step 2 evaluates to $P_n\to I_n$, a quasi-isomorphism by exact evaluation [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. By [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective], $I_n$ is K-injective over $A$. (Reindex positive integers by $n\mapsto n-1$.) Thus [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] identifies both $e_nR H^0(QP)$ and $R\Gamma_A(QP_n)$ with the same complex $\Gamma(\mathcal C,I_n)$, using their derived units. Here $e_n$ on $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Ab}))$ is the derived functor of the exact evaluation, computed termwise by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], and the tower transitions give natural maps $e_{n+1}\to e_n$ computed termwise in the same way. This specifies $\beta_n:e_nR H^0\cong R\Gamma_A e_n$. For a derived input morphism, represent it by a chain map between K-injective tower representatives, using [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; the evaluated map computes both sides. Homotopic maps give homotopic section maps, so these identifications are natural and independent of representatives. The same equality on $\Gamma(I_{n+1})\to\Gamma(I_n)$ proves $\beta_n t=R\Gamma_A(t)\beta_{n+1}$ for the actual tower transitions.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, proof paragraph beginning with the exact left adjoint to evaluation; constant ring-sheaf module version via the cited general tower-evaluation theorem.

proof.text: Write $H_R=R\Gamma(\mathcal C,-):D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))\to D(\operatorname{Ab})$ and $\eta_R$ for its derived unit. For a ring-sheaf map $R\to S$, let $r_{R,S}$ be exact restriction. The underived equality $\Gamma_R r_{R,S}=\Gamma_S$ and the universal property in [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] give a unique comparison $\sigma_{R,S}:H_S\to H_Rr_{R,S}$ with $\sigma_{R,S,Q M}\eta_{S,M}=\eta_{R,r_{R,S}M}$ for every complex $M$. It is invertible: [lem-weil-pbc-restriction-ringed-topos-module-direct-image] realizes $r_{R,S}$ as the direct image of $(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),S)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)$. Compose with the global-sections ringed-topos morphism $g$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] to the one-point site with ring $\underline{\mathbf Z}$, whose module complexes are abelian-group complexes by [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison]: $g^{-1}$ sends a set $E$ to the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], which preserves finite limits as the sheafification of a finite-limit-preserving constant presheaf; $g_*F=\operatorname{Hom}(*,F)=\Gamma(\mathcal C,F)$ is its right adjoint by the universal property of sheafification; the ring map is the unit $\underline{\mathbf Z}\to R$. Thus $g_*$ on $R$-modules is $\Gamma_R$. For an $S$-K-injective $L$ and an $R$-K-injective resolution $j:r_{R,S}L\to K$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] says that $\Gamma(j)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The unit equation computes $\sigma_{R,S,QL}$ by precisely $\Gamma(j)$ under the resolution identifications. It is therefore the canonical composition isomorphism; every derived object has such an $L$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Exact restriction and its right derived functor agree termwise by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Take $R=A,S=B_n$ and use $\sigma_{A,B_n}^{-1}$ after $\beta_n$ to obtain the second required comparison.

proof.text: The scalar comparisons have the needed composition normalization. For $R\to S\to T$, identify $r_{R,S}r_{S,T}=r_{R,T}$ by their identical actions [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Both $\sigma_{R,T}$ and $(\sigma_{R,S}r_{S,T})\sigma_{S,T}$, after precomposition with $\eta_T$, equal $\eta_Rr_{R,T}$ by the unit equations of Step 5. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] therefore makes them equal. The identity-ring comparison is the identity by the same argument. This is a direct application of the cited universal property, rather than an additional coefficient-coherence assumption.

proof.text:
Put $C=B_{n+1}$, $S=B_n$, and let $d:J_{n+1}\to r_{C,S}J_n$ be the given transition in $D(C)$. Its derived-sections map is $\sigma_{C,S,J_n}^{-1}H_C(d):H_C(J_{n+1})\to H_S(J_n)$. Naturality of $\sigma_{A,C}$ in $d$ and Step 6 give the explicit identity
$$\sigma_{A,S,J_n}^{-1}H_A(r_{A,C}d)\sigma_{A,C,J_{n+1}}=\sigma_{C,S,J_n}^{-1}H_C(d).$$
Indeed, substitute $\sigma_{A,S}=(\sigma_{A,C}r_{C,S})\sigma_{C,S}$ and cancel the adjacent inverse comparisons using naturality. Combine this identity with the $\beta$ transition equation of Step 4. The comparisons $\sigma_{A,B_n}^{-1}\beta_n$ thus intertwine the actual transitions of $G(J)$ with the stated finite derived-sections transitions. Every comparison is natural for derived input morphisms by Steps 4 and 5, so their composites are natural too. This calculation applies also to identity and iterated transitions. It only uses K-injectivity of constant-$A$ tower evaluations, never of varying-ring evaluations.
